relay.brief:
The morning guard has counted unmarked transports on three adjoining streets. Imperial troops are closing on the Temple's outer gate, and civilians are still crossing the plaza behind your line. Kira Venn is at the barricade. Tor Saalen is locking the inner passages and moving apprentices, patients, and archive staff away from the entrance. The lock sequence needs six turns to finish.
Hold the approach for all six; if the enemy crosses it early, the guard will have no secure place to regroup. Use the stone planters for cover and keep the center lane watched. Your squad can include Jedi and soldiers, but every person you send must be ready to stay on the line while others withdraw. Do not pursue the attackers into the city.
The objective is time — six turns for the gate, and six turns for everyone behind it. Kira will hold the first position until your squad arrives. Choose their loadout before you deploy.
relay.win:
The sixth turn ends with the inner doors locked and the outer barricade still in Jedi hands. Tor's guard moves the last civilians inside while Kira checks the plaza for anyone left behind. The attackers withdraw down the avenue, leaving damaged transports and unanswered questions. For a moment the Temple's windows hold only the morning sky. Zym thanks the squad by name and orders the gate repaired before nightfall.
Gnost-Dural asks for every recovered signal and insignia; he wants to know who sent the force and why it chose this hour. The Council vision remains sealed, but the people who stood at the gate understand its warning more clearly now. They have proven the Temple can be defended. They have also seen how little time a warning gives them.
relay.lose:
The attackers break the outer line before Tor can finish sealing the inner doors. Kira orders a retreat through smoke and falling stone, keeping the wounded between the squad and the entrance. Temple guards hold the stairwell long enough for the younglings and patients to reach shelter, but the plaza is lost. The Council can see the breach from its chamber; no one says the word vision aloud.
Zym orders the surviving squad to report and assigns every available guard to the inner corridors. Gnost-Dural begins moving irreplaceable records that cannot be left behind. The enemy now knows a route into the Temple, and the Order has paid for that knowledge in lives. There is still time to answer the larger threat, but the next mission begins under a shadow that was only a warning this morning.

envoy.brief:
The peace talks have a leak. A Republic envoy has been passing the delegation's schedule to Imperial handlers through terminals in the lower city. The Council needs proof before it can warn the negotiators without exposing its own sources. Two copied terminals will establish the route; the third may reveal who paid him. A Jedi or Medic must stand beside a terminal to scan it, and one squad member must reach an evacuation zone with the data.
The envoy is still in the district. Capture him if the chance comes, but a prisoner is worth less than the records if the network wipes them. Kira asks you to watch the exits while Tor follows the transmission path from the Temple. The operation will make the coming treaty safer only if someone brings the evidence home before the trail goes cold.
envoy.win:
The copied records reach the Council before the envoy's handlers can erase them. Tor maps a chain of messages from the lower city to an Imperial contact whose cover predates the peace talks. Gnost-Dural reads the timings twice and finds a gap that suggests other orders were sent without the envoy's knowledge. The Senate will be warned through a narrow channel; a public accusation would scatter the network before the Order can trace it.
Kira remembers the families at the gate and asks whether this leak explains that attack. The evidence does not answer her yet. It does show that the Empire is preparing around the treaty rather than waiting to see what peace brings. Your squad has turned a rumor into a warning the Council can act on.
envoy.lose:
The terminals are wiped as the squad reaches them, and the envoy disappears into the lower city. The Council is left with fragments: a departure time, an encrypted address, and a pattern of contacts too broad to name one handler. The delegation will receive a warning, but without proof the Senate may dismiss it as another reason for the Jedi to distrust the treaty. Tor takes the failure personally; the signal crossed a route he believed secured.
Kira reminds him that the squad made it out and that the Empire spent effort to erase its own trail. That is evidence of intent, if not of names. Gnost-Dural preserves every fragment. The next lead may come from older records rather than the network the envoy has abandoned.

vault.brief:
Gnost-Dural has found a sealed archive beneath the Ossus ruins. Its records describe the last strike against a Jedi Temple, and he believes the pattern may explain the Empire's present movements. Imperial agents reached the site first. Your squad begins concealed among broken halls while patrols search the surface. A Jedi or Medic can copy the terminals from beside them; retrieve at least two of three, then send anyone carrying the data to an evacuation zone.
The third terminal may hold a name the others omit. An Acolyte guards the inner chamber, and a prolonged fight gives the agents time to smash what they cannot steal. Tor can guide the extraction, but he cannot retrieve a record buried under a collapsed vault. Go quietly where possible. Bring home the history before another faction decides what survives.
vault.win:
Two archives make it home, and Gnost-Dural remains awake through the night comparing their dates with the envoy's signals. He finds a sequence that is disturbingly familiar: a quiet probe, a diversion near peace talks, and a decisive strike when defenders expect negotiations to buy time. The third terminal, if recovered, adds detail, but the first two are enough to change the Council's plans.
Zym authorizes a broader watch around the Temple and asks Tor to revise every evacuation route. Kira studies the maps with the memory of the outer gate still fresh. The records do not say the future is fixed. They say the Sith have used patience as a weapon before. Your squad has given the Order a chance to recognize that weapon before it lands.
vault.lose:
Fire takes the vault before the squad can extract its records. On the return flight, Gnost-Dural asks for every detail the team remembers: the inscriptions, the terminal positions, even the order in which the agents destroyed them. He copies the account into the Archives beside a blank entry for what Ossus might have told them. Tor can still strengthen the Temple, but without the old record he cannot distinguish a familiar Sith tactic from a coincidence.
Kira argues that the enemy's willingness to burn a site proves it mattered. Zym agrees, and assigns another search to any surviving Imperial transmission. The loss is more than missing lore. It is a warning that the Sith can deny the Order its own memory, one site at a time.

ilum.brief:
A blunt signal from Sergeant Jace Malcom reaches the Temple through a snowstorm: Sith raiders are circling the crystal caves on Ilum. His platoon has the mouth, but not enough people to hold three waves alone. If the raiders enter, they can take the kyber the Order needs for future Jedi blades and threaten the gatherers still deeper in the caves. Hold the mouth for eight turns until relief lands.
The final wave is expected to bring an Acolyte, so keep a reserve rather than spending everyone at the first sight of movement. Malcom knows the terrain and will tell your squad where the wind hides an approach. The Council cannot replace a lost cave with credits. This mission protects a place generations of Jedi have trusted, and the people now sheltering inside it.
ilum.win:
Relief ships come down through the snow as the final raiders retreat. Malcom meets the squad at the cave mouth, his armor rimed white, and points out the narrow paths the enemy almost reached. Gatherers emerge only after the entrance has been checked twice. Some carry crystals; most carry stories of guards who stood in the storm so they did not have to. Zym orders a permanent watch until the route is safe.
Kira sends Malcom a brief note of thanks, and he replies with a list of practical repairs rather than ceremony. Ilum has not become peaceful overnight, but its caves remain open to the Order. The raiders failed to take the kyber or force the Jedi to abandon the young people inside.
ilum.lose:
The last wave reaches the cave mouth before relief can land. Malcom pulls his remaining troopers back around the gatherers, but the raiders enter passages that have never needed a military guard. The Order loses crystals, records of safe routes, and the trust of families who believed Ilum was beyond the war. Zym sends ships to recover whoever can be found and refuses to describe the caves as lost until the search ends.
Kira reads Malcom's terse casualty report twice; he did everything a thin line could do. The Council now must protect other kyber sites before the Sith repeat the move. A failure here will be felt every time a new Jedi asks where to find a crystal and receives no simple answer.

adraasHunt.brief:
Satele Shan has followed Lord Adraas to an embassy hangar on Alderaan. Delegates speak of peace above ground while Adraas waits beside a fueled shuttle for a signal he expects soon. Satele believes he is part of a strike force aimed at the Temple. Your squad enters concealed and must defeat him before he reaches the shuttle.
The hangar gives him cover and an escape route, and the noise of a long fight may bring security who cannot tell one faction from another. Kira asks whether the Council can act in a diplomatic building without risking the treaty. Zym answers that a treaty cannot excuse an attack already being prepared. Keep the fight contained, protect anyone caught in the hangar, and leave with evidence of Adraas's orders if you can.
Every minute he remains free is another minute for the signal to arrive.
adraasHunt.win:
Adraas falls before the shuttle can lift. Satele checks the hangar for surviving crew and finds orders that connect his arrival to movements around Coruscant. The Embassy will demand an explanation, and the Council will have to give one without surrendering its source. For now, the most urgent fact is simpler: one leader has been removed from the force moving toward the Temple. Kira and Tor compare the recovered timings with the gate assault and the envoy's messages.
The pattern sharpens into a plan. Satele knows this victory cannot end the strike by itself, but she sees the difference it makes to the people who will stand at Docking Ring Nine. There will be one fewer blade waiting for them there.
adraasHunt.lose:
Adraas reaches his shuttle and lifts into Alderaan's bright sky before the squad can stop him. Satele watches its vector until it disappears from the tactical display, then gathers everyone who survived the hangar fight. The Council has evidence of his intent, but no certainty about where he will land next. Tor warns every Temple approach and Kira reviews the gate guard's new positions.
The treaty delegates continue their work, unaware that a Sith Lord has left their city for a different kind of negotiation. Zym does not blame the squad for an enemy escape; he asks what it learned. Adraas now knows the Order is watching him, and he may adapt. The Temple must prepare for the strike as though his blade will be in it.

dock.brief:
The treaty is being signed on Alderaan. On Coruscant, Darth Malgus lands at Docking Ring Nine with a strike team whose path leads to the Temple lifts. The Council's sealed vision has become painfully close to a military timetable. Your squad must defeat Malgus before he reaches the lifts; if the threat rises too far, he will break through. Fuel barrels in the ring can be used as hazards, but civilians and allies may be near them.
Kira has the Temple guard ready behind you, and Tor is holding the inner routes closed. Neither can stop Malgus if the docking ring falls. Fight for position, keep your people together, and deny him the straight path toward the lifts. This is the moment the earlier clues pointed to. The Order has prepared as well as it could. Now the defense depends on the squad you send.
dock.win:
Malgus falls on the docking ring, far enough from the Temple that the people inside hear only a distant report of the battle. Kira confirms the lifts are secure and Tor begins the slow work of reopening routes that were sealed against a catastrophe. The treaty ceremony continues under a shadow its delegates do not yet understand. Zym brings the squad before the Council, not to declare the Sith threat finished, but to record what their choices prevented.
Gnost-Dural places the gate assault, the envoy's trail, and the Ossus records beside the battle account. Together they show how close the strike came and how many hands helped stop it. The vision was a warning. Today, the Temple did not burn as it showed.
dock.lose:
Malgus breaks through the docking ring and reaches the Temple lifts. Tor orders every inner barrier sealed; Kira takes the surviving guard to the next defensible position. Smoke climbs the shaft, and the Council's vision feels less like a distant possibility than a record being written in real time. Zym sends the younglings away from the central halls and stays to direct the defense. The squad's effort bought some time, but not enough to keep the strike outside.
Gnost-Dural preserves the evidence that led them here, because even a failed warning must teach the Order what to do next. The Temple's fate is not decided by this one retreat. What is certain is that the war has entered a place the Jedi believed they could still protect.

r_muster.brief:
Lord Hoth is bringing the Army of Light down to Ruusan, and the Brotherhood knows exactly which landing field his transports need. The beacon is the only clear guide through smoke and broken weather. Hold it for seven turns so the ships can find the ground without scattering across enemy lines. The last assault is expected to arrive behind a Sith Lord whose presence steadies nearby troopers, so leave room to reposition when the first wave breaks.
Troops at the beacon can protect the approach; Jedi can meet the enemy command before it reaches the signal. The Army cannot begin its campaign if half its strength lands in the wrong valley. Hoth has put lives and strategy in your hands. Keep the light visible until the final transport is down.
r_muster.win:
The seventh turn ends with engines overhead and the beacon still burning. Hoth's transports descend through the smoke, one after another, until the field is crowded with soldiers who know how close they came to landing blind. The Brotherhood withdraws before the Army can form a full line. Hoth asks for the squad that held the signal and gives them no grand speech, only the position of the next danger.
Johun, his student, helps carry the wounded from the field and remembers the people who kept the route open. Ruusan is now a battlefield the Army can contest rather than a trap it fell into. The victory buys a beginning, not an ending, and every ship on the ground makes the next choice possible.
r_muster.lose:
The beacon goes dark before the final transports can descend. Pilots scatter toward valleys they cannot see clearly, and Hoth spends the first hours of the campaign gathering survivors instead of forming a line. The squad pulls back from the field with the signal equipment it can save. Johun helps count the missing ships; each number is a unit the Army expected to have at its side.
Hoth refuses to abandon the operation, but his first plan is gone. The Brotherhood has learned how to make one small position matter to an entire campaign. The Temple records the cost without softening it. Ruusan can still be fought for, yet the Army enters its next battle divided, tired, and already behind the enemy's timetable.

r_ravine.brief:
A Brotherhood sweep is coming down the ravine below Hoth's line. His wounded are still inside a field hospital, and among them is Johun Othone, the student who stayed behind to help others move. The north evacuation route is open for now. Escort Johun there; the squad may have to slow down to keep the injured together. After six turns, more troopers are expected, and they have been ordered to shoot the wounded on sight.
There is no honor to be won by holding an empty ravine after the last stretcher leaves. Keep a path through cover, watch the rear, and send someone ahead to make the evacuation zone safe. Hoth knows his student chose to stay. He is trusting you to make sure that choice does not become a sentence.
r_ravine.win:
Johun reaches the evacuation route with the wounded who could still be moved. The hospital tent is empty when the Brotherhood sweep arrives, its instruments packed or broken so they cannot be used against anyone left behind. Hoth meets the convoy without hiding his relief. He thanks the squad for his student, then makes himself thank them again for every unnamed soldier beside him. Johun has seen what a retreat costs and what careful protection can save.
That memory will shape the way he speaks about the war long after the ravine is forgotten by commanders. The Temple adds the rescued names to its record. On Ruusan, saving a life has become a tactical act and a promise about what kind of army the Jedi mean to be.
r_ravine.lose:
The sweep reaches the hospital before Johun can be taken north. The squad saves those it can and leaves the ravine under fire, with empty stretchers where people should have been. Hoth receives the account in silence and asks for the names before he asks for a map. He knows his student stayed to move the wounded; he also knows that bravery alone cannot open a blocked route.
The Brotherhood's order to shoot patients is sent to the Council as evidence of what its war has become. No one uses the loss to make a clean speech about sacrifice. The Army must prepare another evacuation line and protect its hospitals with the same attention it gives its guns. The ravine remains a place the survivors will remember.

r_caves.brief:
A prisoner says the Brotherhood is gathering in the cave network below Ruusan. Tablets inside describe a ritual, but the report is incomplete and Kaan's people are already moving to destroy the evidence. Copy at least two of the three tablets with a Jedi or Medic beside them, then reach an evacuation zone with the records. The third may explain the final step.
Something in the dark hunts Jedi and passes over ordinary soldiers, so do not send a Force user alone into a blind passage. Threat rises after six turns, when the tablets begin to vanish. Hoth needs to know whether Kaan is assembling an army or preparing something no army could survive. The squad is there to bring back an answer, not to clear every chamber. Leave with the records while there is still a way out.
r_caves.win:
The tablets reach the Council, and their translation changes the atmosphere of every command meeting. Kaan is not merely calling his Lords together. He is shaping a ritual that could consume the forces on both sides of the war. Hoth reads the report and asks for confirmation before committing lives to the caves. Gnost-Dural finds older references in the Temple archive, each incomplete but close enough to make dismissal impossible.
The squad's account of the creature that stalked Jedi becomes part of the warning too. The Brotherhood has made the terrain itself hostile to those most likely to stop it. With the records safe, the Army can plan an approach that treats the ritual as the objective rather than a rumor beneath the battlefield.
r_caves.lose:
The caves collapse and the tablets are lost before the squad can extract a usable copy. Survivors bring back impressions of symbols, shouted orders, and a presence that seemed to follow Jedi through the dark. Hoth cannot order an assault on impressions alone, yet he cannot ignore the prisoner's warning either. The Council searches its archives for the ritual's shape and finds gaps where certainty would have been useful.
Johun asks whether another team should enter; Hoth says the Brotherhood will now expect it. The enemy has bought secrecy with stone and fire. The Army must prepare for a threat it cannot describe, while the squad's account remains the only witness to what Kaan was writing beneath Ruusan.

r_sixth.brief:
The sixth battle of Ruusan has left the Army of Light scattered. Brotherhood troops dragged Lord Tarsus Vell from the field and locked him in a stockade before Kaan can make an example of him. His cell can be opened by a Medic hacking from four tiles away or by a Jedi at the console. Once the door opens, get Vell to an evacuation zone; a freed prisoner is still vulnerable in the open.
Threat rises after turn five, and at its peak the guards march him out of reach. The stockade may tempt the squad into a stand, but extraction is the mission. Hoth needs Vell's knowledge of the line and the men who followed him need proof he has not been abandoned. Bring him out before Kaan decides his fate.
r_sixth.win:
Vell comes through the evacuation route exhausted and furious, but alive. Hoth lets him speak first. He describes where the Brotherhood line was thin, where the Army mistook a retreat for a collapse, and how quickly a prisoner becomes a weapon in Kaan's hands. Johun records the details while healers treat injuries Vell tried to hide. The soldiers who thought their Lord lost see him return because a squad went into the stockade for one person.
That knowledge matters after a battle that taught them to expect abandonment. Vell owes the Temple his life and is plain about the debt. Hoth is plainer: the next battle must use what Vell learned, or the rescue will have saved only a witness to another defeat.
r_sixth.lose:
Vell is gone by the time the squad reaches the cell. The guards march him toward Kaan, leaving a stockade that feels empty even while it remains defended. Hoth's officers can no longer assume their captured Lord will return, and the soldiers who followed him look for an answer no commander can give. Johun takes the squad's account, including every route that was tried and every moment the alarm moved ahead of them.
He wants to know whether a second rescue is possible. Hoth cannot promise it; the Brotherhood has learned what the Jedi value. The loss forces a hard change in the Army's planning: future retreats must include a way to recover the wounded and captured before the enemy can turn them into symbols.

r_seventh.brief:
The seventh battle begins against Kaan's line on the high ground. Lord Vorr holds the ledge that lets Brotherhood marksmen rake the Army's advance. Defeat him, and Hoth's forces can push through the gap before the line closes again. Threat rises after six turns; when it peaks, the attack fails even if your squad survives below the ledge. Fuel barrels near the position can break cover when shot, but their blast may catch anyone too close.
Johun reports that the Army is ready to move the moment Vorr falls. Your squad's task is to make that moment happen. Hoth cannot spend another day feeding soldiers into the same uphill approach. Break the command holding the ledge and give the rest of the Army a path forward.
r_seventh.win:
Vorr falls, and the change travels down Kaan's line faster than any order. Brotherhood troopers abandon the ledge, then the positions below it, until Hoth can send the Army through ground that had cost it too many attempts. Johun moves with the advance, carrying messages and watching for wounded on both sides of the broken line.
The victory is loud on the field but quiet in the Temple's record: one commander removed, one path opened, many lives spared from a longer assault. Hoth knows Kaan's remaining forces will gather in the caves. The squad has not ended the Ruusan campaign. It has taken away the ground that let the Brotherhood pretend the campaign could remain a conventional battle.
r_seventh.lose:
Vorr holds the ledge until the Army's attack loses momentum. Hoth orders his soldiers back rather than spend them against a position that has survived its best chance to break. The squad returns through ground marked by repeated assaults; every retreat route is familiar now. Johun carries casualty names to the healers and will not let the staff reduce them to numbers on a map.
Kaan's line remains between the Army and the caves, buying the Brotherhood more time for whatever it is preparing there. The defeat is tactical and immediate, but its larger cost is time. Hoth must find another way up the slope while the Council measures how close the ritual may be to completion.

r_bomb.brief:
Kaan has gathered his Lords at a ritual ground beneath Ruusan. The thought bomb they intend to unleash could destroy Jedi and Sith alike. Hoth is moving into the caves to stop them, but a battlefield victory outside will mean little if the ritual fires first. Defeat Kaan before the threat reaches its final stage.
If Darth Bane is present, decide how to contain him before Kaan falls; he may walk away while every eye is on the bomb. The ground will be crowded with enemies who know they are fighting for an ending, not a retreat. Your squad has records from the caves and the cost of every battle that brought the Army here. Use that knowledge.
Break the ritual, protect Hoth's advance, and keep Ruusan from becoming a grave for both orders.
r_bomb.win:
Kaan falls, and the ritual breaks before its force can gather. For a moment everyone in the cave waits for a sound that never comes. Hoth orders the survivors out into daylight and begins counting the people who did not follow. Johun helps the wounded through the passages while the Army searches for prisoners, records, and any remaining sign of the bomb. The Council will argue over what victory means after so much loss.
On Ruusan, its meaning is immediate. The ground still holds the living, and the sky remains above them. The squad's choices in the caves determine which enemies are gone and which may shape a later age. The Temple records both the lives saved and the dangers that escaped.
r_bomb.lose:
The thought bomb fires before Kaan can be stopped. The cave becomes silent in a way no battlefield should be; the Force itself seems to draw back from what has happened. Hoth's last advance and the squad's effort are swallowed by a ritual that made no distinction between enemies. Johun's earlier reports, the rescued records, and the warnings from the tablets survive only where someone carried them away in time.
The Council cannot answer the loss with a triumphant campaign account. It must care for the survivors and understand how a leader persuaded his own followers to make annihilation a strategy. Ruusan will be remembered for the people who tried to stop the bomb and for the terrible fact that trying was not enough.

h_hetzal.brief:
A ship has broken apart in hyperspace, and its fragments are still falling on Hetzal at impossible speed. Rescue crews cannot stay in the impact fields for long. Masked raiders have reached the wrecks first and are searching them while survivors call for help. One survivor is close enough to reach; escort them to the northern evacuation zone. Raiders will dash back to cover after firing, and a Path-Runner is expected behind your line on turn two.
Do not let the apparent front of the fight leave the evac route unguarded. Marshal Avar Kriss is coordinating a wider rescue, but she cannot see every person in every field. Your squad can bring this one out. Move with the survivor, keep a path open, and leave before the falling wreckage and raiders close it.
h_hetzal.win:
The survivor reaches the evacuation ship with a story of falling metal, masked figures, and a squad that came back through the impact field instead of writing the area off. Avar Kriss asks who those rescuers are and sends their account to the other crews. The raiders were searching particular wrecks, not simply taking anything valuable. That detail gives the Jedi a question to pursue after the immediate rescue ends.
On Hetzal, there is no single clean victory while fragments are still falling. There are people who made it out and people the Order must keep searching for. The squad's success becomes a practical example: follow the distress signal, protect the route home, and treat one life as enough reason to return.
h_hetzal.lose:
The final transport leaves without the survivor the squad was sent to find. The impact field changes under falling debris, and the raiders use the confusion to vanish with whatever they came to take. Avar Kriss receives an account full of coordinates, near misses, and the last place a signal was heard. She sends another rescue team when the field is safe enough, though no one can promise what it will find.
The squad has learned that the masked attackers planned their arrival as carefully as the Republic planned its response. The loss is personal to the people who waited at the evac zone and strategic to an Order that still does not know why the wrecks mattered. Hetzal remains a crisis, and the search continues.

h_grove.brief:
The Drengir are waking in a valley of farms: thinking plants that hunt, bind, and feed. At the center, the Great Progenitor has rooted deep enough to send new growth through the fields. Defeat her before the grove expands beyond the valley. Vines can pin a squad member in place, and another Drengir sprouts near her every three turns, so a slow advance gives the hive more bodies. Farmers are sheltering beyond the line you can see.
They need a safe road out, not a display of courage that leaves the root intact. The Council has little history of fighting a creature that treats the ground itself as an ally. Watch where your squad stands, clear a route for the wounded, and take the fight to the Progenitor before she can turn the whole valley into cover.
h_grove.win:
The Progenitor withers, and the grove goes quiet so suddenly the farmers can hear their own machines again. Then the vines begin to brown. The squad marks every place where a tendril still moves and calls healers for those who were caught in the roots. No one declares the valley safe on the first day; fields that held the hive must be checked before families return.
The Council records what the squad learned about the Drengir's rhythm, especially how new growth followed the mother. Avar Kriss sends the report to worlds that may face the same threat. The victory is measured in a road reopened, people returning to their homes, and a pattern others can use before the next grove takes hold.
h_grove.lose:
The grove spreads beyond the farms while the Progenitor remains alive at its center. The squad withdraws with the people it can reach, leaving equipment and fields behind as roots close the road. Families who grew food there watch the valley disappear under a living enemy. The Council must quarantine the area and learn how to fight a hive that can replace its losses faster than an ordinary force.
Avar Kriss asks for every observation, because other worlds may already be seeing the first signs of Drengir growth. The failure cannot be contained in one mission report. It changes where people can live and how safely they can travel. The Order will have to return with a stronger plan before the grove reaches another settlement.

h_valo.brief:
The Republic Fair at Valo was built to show the frontier what cooperation can make. Now the Nihil have come to burn that promise in front of the galaxy. Crowds are still leaving the grounds, and Chancellor Lina Soh's pavilion is the last defensible point on their route. Hold it for seven turns. Path-Runners can appear behind your line, while Storms use choking gas to drive defenders from cover.
A squad that watches only the main entrance will lose the people it was sent to protect. The Chancellor's guard can move civilians, but it needs the pavilion to remain standing while the last groups pass. The cameras will record the battle, yet the objective is not an image. It is a clear exit for people who came to a fair and found a war.
h_valo.win:
The pavilion stands through the seventh turn. Lina Soh walks out of the smoke and thanks the defenders by name, then turns to the evac crews still working beyond the lights. Footage of the fair will cross the holonet, including the Nihil attack and the people who helped strangers reach safety. The Republic cannot pretend the frontier is secure simply because the Chancellor survived.
Avar Kriss asks for the squad's account of the Path-Runners and gas teams so other worlds can prepare. Valo's victory is imperfect: stalls are burned, people are missing, and the celebration is over. Still, the evacuation route held. The promise the fair tried to make now has a harder form: when danger came, someone stayed long enough for others to leave.
h_valo.lose:
The pavilion burns while the evacuation is still underway. Its collapse becomes the image shown on every holonet channel, but the people who were there remember more than a picture: gas in the walkways, sudden attackers behind the line, and a route that closed too soon. Lina Soh survives or is carried from the grounds by her guard, and must speak for a Republic that could not keep its own fair safe.
Avar Kriss directs the search for the missing before any public accounting begins. The Nihil wanted spectacle, and they have it. The Order cannot undo the image, but it can learn from the attack and bring the same attention to less visible places where families are now asking whether help will reach them in time.

h_tempest.brief:
Evidence from Valo points to a Nihil hideout at the edge of Wild Space. Lourna Dee, one of the Tempest Runners, is there long enough for a strike if the squad moves quickly. Defeat her before her ship jumps. At half strength she can Path-jump to a new position and recover, so do not mistake the first opening for the end of the fight. A drawn-out battle raises the threat until she escapes.
The hideout may contain routes to other raids, but its most urgent value is the leader directing them. Avar Kriss wants her alive if that can be done without losing the chance to stop her. Your squad must watch the exits, keep pressure after she relocates, and leave the Nihil without one of the people who made Valo possible.
h_tempest.win:
Lourna Dee goes down before her ship can jump. The hideout yields routes, stores, and orders that turn scattered Nihil attacks into a map the Jedi can study. Avar Kriss sends the most urgent leads to worlds still cleaning up after Valo. Capturing or defeating a Tempest Runner does not make the Nihil disappear; their raids were built to continue when a leader is lost.
It does force them to adapt while the Republic has a chance to prepare. The squad returns with wounds and hard evidence instead of another rumor. For the families who watched the fair burn, this victory cannot repair everything. It can show that the people who planned that attack are within reach and can be stopped.
h_tempest.lose:
Lourna Dee's ship jumps before the squad can secure the hideout. She has seen their faces and learned how they close a trap; the next encounter will begin with that knowledge on her side. Avar Kriss takes the partial route data the team recovered and sends warnings to the likely targets. Some coordinates may be decoys left during the retreat. The squad's fight has still disrupted one operation, but the Nihil leader remains free to choose another.
Valo's survivors will ask whether the Jedi caught the person responsible. The answer is no, and the Council will have to live with it while planning the next move. A failed interception is a lesson only if its details are recorded before anger turns them into a simple story.

h_husks.brief:
Three Jedi entered an abandoned outpost. Their comlinks still answer, but the figures standing in its corridors are gray as stone and crumble when touched. The logs may explain what happened and whether the danger can travel. Copy at least two of three terminals with a Jedi or Medic beside them, then reach an evacuation zone. A third log may name the thing responsible.
The Nameless harms Jedi while ordinary troops are immune, so let soldiers test unknown ground and keep Force users from walking blind into the center. The mission is an investigation under threat, not a search for a conventional enemy to defeat. Bring the records out even if every instinct says to stay and help the Jedi you found. The Order cannot protect the next team without knowing what made them hollow.
h_husks.win:
The logs name the creature. It is a Nameless, held by Marchion Ro and used against Jedi. Avar Kriss receives the report with visible effort; the gray figures in the outpost were colleagues, not specimens. The Council sends a warning that changes squad planning across the frontier: ordinary troops can approach where Jedi cannot, and courage does not cancel the creature's effect. The recovered terminals also show when the outpost fell, narrowing the path Ro took afterward.
The squad has brought home more than evidence. It has given the Order a way to speak honestly about a threat it had no name for yesterday. The outpost remains a place of loss, but the people who died there may keep others from entering the same trap unprepared.
h_husks.lose:
The outpost goes dark before the squad can bring out enough logs to explain the gray figures. Avar Kriss orders its location marked and forbids another Jedi team from entering without a different plan. Survivors describe an enemy they could barely perceive and comrades who crumbled at a touch. Those details are terrifying precisely because they do not yet form an answer.
The Council cannot tell families what happened to the three Jedi beyond the evidence it has, and it will not invent a comforting account. Ordinary troops who returned from the corridors offer to guide a future mission; they noticed the danger did not strike them in the same way. The Order has a clue, a loss, and an obligation to investigate before the threat reaches another station.

h_beacon.brief:
The Nihil are inside Starlight Beacon. Systems are failing across the station, and the Nameless is turning Jedi to dust where they try to intervene. Marchion Ro has come to watch it fall. Defeat him before the threat reaches its final stage and the Beacon loses orbit. The Leveler harms Jedi while ordinary troops can endure its presence; use that difference to protect your Force users without leaving the squad divided.
Ro marks the people he shoots, making every exposed position more dangerous. Avar Kriss is coordinating evacuation while the station still has power, but she cannot repair it if Ro keeps control of the attack. The Beacon was built as a promise to distant worlds. Today that promise has weight, corridors, and people inside it. Hold them long enough to stop the fall.
h_beacon.win:
Ro falls on the station he meant to destroy, and Starlight holds its orbit. The rescue work continues long after the fight is over: engineers isolate damaged decks, medics search sealed rooms, and Avar Kriss sends ships to carry people away before any system fails again. The Leveler's presence is recorded with care, because defeating its master does not make the knowledge of it harmless.
The Council will debate what Starlight now means to the Republic and whether it can be restored. For those who were aboard, the answer begins with a simpler fact: the station stayed in the sky long enough for them to leave it. The squad has ended Ro's attack, but it must also remember the people whose losses made the victory possible.
h_beacon.lose:
Starlight Beacon falls. The last signals from its decks carry names, coordinates, and voices trying to guide others toward escape pods. Avar Kriss orders every available ship to the debris field and refuses to call the search finished while a rescue beacon still answers. Ro's attack has destroyed a station that was meant to make the frontier feel less distant from the Republic.
The Nameless leaves the Jedi with a fear they must learn to understand without letting it define them. The Council's record will include the squad's attempt, the people saved, and the failure to stop the fall. No sentence can make the loss smaller. The work that follows is to carry survivors home and decide how to face a galaxy that has seen its brightest beacon go dark.

events.e1_gnost_archive:
Master Gnost-Dural arrives with a request he has been refining since the Council saw the Temple burn. He wants a full copy of the Archives sent to a hidden colony, with names and coordinates kept out of ordinary dispatches. The work would draw funds and archivists from repairs the Temple needs now. Zym asks him whether he believes the vision is certain. Gnost-Dural says certainty is the wrong standard for a record that can be lost only once.
Other Masters worry that moving copies in secret would tell the Order to expect defeat and might expose the colony if a courier is followed. The chamber looks to you because your squads would protect the route. Approving the copy makes a practical promise to future Jedi; refusing keeps those people and resources at the Temple today. Gnost-Dural is listening to how you weigh both duties.
events.e1_kyber_trade:
A Hutt broker offers Ilum-grade kyber crystals through an intermediary who refuses to name the mine. The quality is real; the price is permission to let a spice shipment pass a Republic checkpoint without Jedi scrutiny. The broker calls it a harmless trade between powers that already look away when convenient. A healer in the chamber has treated people harmed by that same route.
Another Councilor points out that the crystals could arm young Jedi before the next Sith raid. Seizing the cargo would make the Order an active party in the broker's territory, with all the retaliation that might follow. The Council has no clean account of how he obtained the kyber. It does have a clear account of what he is asking in exchange.
Your decision will be remembered by the people who receive the crystals and by those who live along the spice run.
events.e1_mando_blockade:
Mandalorian ships in Imperial pay have closed a supply lane used by Republic relief convoys. The Navy asks the Order for a squad that can break the blockade; the Senate asks Jedi to stay out while it negotiates. A quartermaster lays out the cargo already delayed: medicine, repair parts, and food meant for settlements still recovering from the war.
Paying the clans could reopen the route quickly, but it would teach them that the same threat can earn another payment next month. Sending a squad risks a fight that the Senate will call unauthorized. Ignoring the lane leaves the settlements to absorb the cost of a political argument being held far away from them. Tor has marked possible insertion points and waits for your order. The Council wants to know which obligation you will treat as urgent.
events.e1_treaty_vote:
The evidence from your missions points toward a strike timed to the peace treaty. The Council must decide who hears the warning before the delegates gather. The Senate can move guards and change routes, but its offices contain people whose loyalties the Order has not settled. A broad warning could travel to Imperial agents as quickly as it reaches the delegation.
Keeping the intelligence inside the Temple preserves the element of surprise and leaves civilian authorities with less time to protect their own people. Zym asks you to speak from what the squad found, not from the sealed vision. Kira says the people at the gate were not told enough to choose where to stand. Tor replies that revealing a defense can break it. Neither is making the choice lightly.
The room waits for a recommendation that can be acted on before the treaty begins.
events.e1_satele:
Satele Shan asks to join the Temple's strike teams. She has followed the same clues your squad has and believes she can help before the Empire turns them into another attack. Her master, Kao Cen Darach, objects. He knows her skill; his concern is that she is taking on a war at the exact moment she should be learning when to refuse its pull.
Satele answers that waiting at a safe distance will not make the decisions easier later. The Council can take her into the field, gaining a capable Knight while straining its trust with Darach, or respect his judgment and leave her on her current path. Zym asks Satele to remain for the decision so it is spoken to her rather than about her. What you choose will shape more than one mission roster.
events.e1_prisoner_offer:
A captured Imperial officer offers names of Republic traitors in exchange for a ship and a route beyond the Navy's reach. He has given one verifiable detail, enough to prove access but not enough to prove the rest. The Navy wants custody and a formal interrogation. Tor believes the officer's contacts may be preparing for the treaty, while Kira asks what becomes of the people he names if he is lying to save himself.
Pressing him by force might yield faster answers and leave a Jedi carrying the cost of how they were obtained. A deal would give an enemy freedom and perhaps give the Council a map of the network. The chamber has to decide how much uncertainty it will buy, who will bear the risk, and whether the method used to learn the truth can survive being entered in the Temple record.
events.e1_refugees:
Families from Taris have reached the Temple after weeks of moving between temporary shelters. They ask to sleep in the gardens, where there is water, a medical wing, and enough open ground to keep their children together. The Senate says that using the Temple as a camp would set a bad example and make it harder to turn away the next group. A healer replies that the next group is already at the door.
Taking them in costs supplies and political favor, but it also gives the Order a chance to help people whose homes are gone. Sending them to the Senate may secure an official answer after another night outside. Turning them away closes the question for the Council and opens it for everyone who watched the gate. You can see the families from the chamber window as the vote begins.
events.e1_senate_audit:
A Senate committee demands an account of every credit the Order has spent on the war. Its letter cites legitimate public concerns alongside line items that could reveal where squads and safehouses operate. Opening the books would require clerks to prepare a version that protects people without hiding mistakes. Refusal would be faster, and it would confirm the suspicion of Senators who think the Temple answers only to itself.
The quartermaster admits that some emergency spending was recorded badly during the gate attack. Zym says the Order must be able to explain its stewardship, even when the question is asked for political reasons. Tor asks that no name in a covert route be made public by accident. The Council needs a decision that can be implemented by people who will sit with the ledger long after this meeting ends.
events.e1_ilum_call:
Sergeant Jace Malcom sends a short signal from Ilum. Sith scouts are circling the crystal caves, and his platoon has too few people to watch every mouth. He asks for help without dressing the request as a plea. Sending money for kyber protection could strengthen the cave guard and supply future Jedi, but it will not put a squad on the snow today.
Promising help may steady Malcom's people while binding the Order to a response it must actually deliver. The Council knows Ilum as a place of gathering and apprenticeship; Malcom describes it as a set of approaches, blind turns, and lines that can fail. Zym asks you to hear both descriptions. The decision before you is small compared with the battle Malcom may face, but the answer will reach him before the next storm clears.
events.e1_defector:
An Imperial agent asks to defect. She says she knows how strike teams receive orders and which relay carries their messages near Republic space. The SIS offers to take custody immediately and share what it can verify later. Tor warns that turning her over may bury details the Temple needs now. Kira asks what guarantee the agent has that the Order will protect her if her information proves incomplete.
Bringing her in could reveal the network, but a planted defector could wound the person assigned to lead the interview and escape with a map of Temple procedures. The Council cannot test every claim before choosing where she goes. Zym asks for a decision that includes the cost to the people who will receive her. She is waiting in a guarded room and knows her window to leave the Empire is closing.
